ledger.note: 338: Cuan Chen takes control of Yunnan. 'Cuan Chen of the Cuanman gains control over Yunnan' (Timeline of Yunnan-Guizhou, 338); the Cuanman page: 'In 339, Cuan Chen established garrisons in Nanzhong (present-day Yunnan and western Guizhou)'. Counterpart 'nobody': neither page names who held the land (Eastern Jin's Ning Province or Cheng-Han).

570: Cuan Zan divides his realm between his sons. 'Cuan Zan splits his realm into the Wuman/Black Mywa, ruled by his son Cuan Zhen, in the east', and the White Mywa under his eldest son Cuan Wan in the west (Timeline); the Cuanman page: 'split into Baiman and Wuman' in 602. Both halves stay under Cuan rulers and one colour (keyframe cuan-clan_338). [Reviewer ea-03-x: type split -> rename; a split would have cut the Qujing disc out of the Cuan shape, against the keyframe.]

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (a clan chiefdom, 'Western Cuan State' in Chinese records). Start 327 is the first dated ruler; the infobox formation date is c. 225 and the page also has the clan migrate in the 320s. 338 (Timeline) against 339 (Cuanman page) for Cuan Chen. 570 (Timeline) against 602 (Cuanman page) for the Baiman and Wuman split. Not on the pages: the Ningzhou (Ning Province) relations with Jin, Cheng-Han (333, ea-03-b), Liu Song, Liang, Northern Zhou (a native of Ningzhou rose in 549, granted Southern Ningzhou), the Sui expeditions' commanders, the Lingnan side. Successors: the Six Zhao of Yunnan (early 7th century) have no dossier; Nanzhao (Cliopatria 741-910) unites them in 737. The Eastern Jin or Cheng-Han dossiers may carry matching Ning Province events. Family china is a placeholder for the colour agent (no family fits a Yunnan chiefdom).
